rules.label: Presumptive eligibility via state/federal programs
rules.quote: Presumptive Eligibility: Eligibility in state or federally funded programs. Examples include housing assistance, food stamps and the Women, Infants & Children program (WIC).

notes: Policy applies only to Vail Health medical bills; services by other providers (Vail Valley Surgery Center, The Steadman Clinic, Vail-Summit Orthopedics & Neurosurgery, Anesthesia Partners Colorado, Cardinal Pathology, Critical Care & Pulmonary Consults, Obstetrics/Pediatrics at Vail Health Hospital excluding CMM providers, Dillon Surgery Center, Steadman Philippon Surgery Center) are excluded.
Financial counselors assist patients in determining eligibility for government-sponsored programs and refer to Colorado health insurance exchange.

After submitting completed application with supporting documentation, patient receives eligibility letter within 60 days; Hospital Discounted Care letters within 14 days of receipt of completed application.
If application received within 240 days of initial billing and deemed incomplete, written notice sent within 15 days requesting missing information within 30 days of notice date.
Denials may be appealed with appeal letter and supporting documents; appeals reviewed within 30 days of receipt.
Once approved for financial assistance or Hospital Discounted Care, patient deemed approved for 12 months subsequent to approval.
If patient granted financial assistance on portion of bill and does not pay remaining portion, Vail Health will not reverse the amount of financial assistance granted.
Patients eligible at less than 250% FPL will not be charged more than amount collected from Vail Health's lowest commercial contracted payer.
Vail Health shall not discriminate based on race, color, national origin, sex, age or disability.
Full FAP and application form available at VailHealth.org/FinancialAssistance.
rule_presumptive may leave out a condition: Policy links presumptive eligibility to government-sponsored programs but does not specify benefit amount.

findings.title: Covers everyone Colorado's Hospital Discounted Care protects

law.source: HCPF Hospital Discounted Care Operations Manual, Mar 31 2026
law.quote: Patients and their households are eligible for Hospital Discounted Care if, during the required screening and application processes, they are determined to: Have a total household income at or below 250% of the Federal Poverty Guidelines (FPG), and Be residents of the State of Colorado.
IF REQUESTED BY THE PATIENT, A HEALTH-CARE FACILITY SHALL SCREEN AN INSURED PATIENT FOR DISCOUNTED CARE

findings.summary: Inconclusive: 1 of the model's rules were dropped by the quote and meaning checks, so a missing rule may be our error. Z3's case: A household of 3 earning $27,000 a year (98.8% of the poverty line), living in Colorado, uninsured meets every requirement, but no rule of this policy grants them help. Colorado law makes them eligible for Hospital Discounted Care.

findings.title: Earning less never means getting less help
findings.summary: Inconclusive: 1 of the model's rules were dropped by the quote and meaning checks, so a missing rule may be our error. Z3's case: A household of 3 earning $68,473 a year (250.6% of the poverty line), living in Colorado, uninsured gets no help; the same household earning more, at 451.00% of the poverty line, gets 50% off. The written income bands leave a gap between them.
